title: OpenAI Codex CLI
denyMechanism: sandbox policy (`--sandbox read-only|workspace-write`) + approval policy in config.toml; no per-skill tool allowlist. `agents/openai.yaml` `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` disables implicit invocation

listing.budget: skills list ≤ 2 % of context or 8 000 chars
listing.note: name + description drive implicit matching; the full SKILL.md loads when selected regardless of budget

degradations.text: skill `allowed-tools` is informational — Codex enforces nothing per skill; only the sandbox/approval policy restricts
a Claude-style agent `tools:` allowlist has no TOML counterpart and is dropped when rendered to .codex/agents/*.toml
`disable-model-invocation` has no effect; use `agents/openai.yaml` policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false

a skill has no /slash invocation and no dedicated tool: Codex lists the skills with their paths and the model READS the chosen SKILL.md, so an invocation is observable only as a file read. Measured on codex-cli 0.153.0 — its hook surface carries no prompt-expansion event (pre_tool_use, permission_request, post_tool_use, pre_compact, post_compact, session_start, session_end, user_prompt_submit, subagent_start, subagent_stop, interrupt) and a slash-prefixed prompt reaches user_prompt_submit as literal text.

sources: measured 2026-09-23: `codex exec -m gpt-5.6` → HTTP 400 on a ChatGPT account (~/lab SKILLS_MODEL_REFRESH_REVIEW §8)
models.note: Codex agents carry the model in TOML (`model`, `model_reasoning_effort`), not in SKILL.md; in a TAUT pack the deployment `modelTiers` ladder is checked. The harness's own catalog on this machine, when present, is consulted first.

catalog.note: no GPT-6 successor; the Codex migration map moves it to gpt-6-sol
the local catalog marks it for upgrade
not in the Codex catalog; a session pinned to it gets HTTP 400 on a ChatGPT account (measured 2026-09-23)
